issues.description: The problem statement's UML and attribute list specify numberOfLecturers as an int, but the solution declares the field as a byte. This is a structural type mismatch for the attribute and deviates from the specification in the problem statement, which can confuse students about the intended type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field type for numberOfLecturers consistent with the UML and problem statement by changing its declaration in the solution to int (i.e., private int numberOfLecturers;). Ensure any related methods and documentation reflect the int type as well.

issues.description: The setter for numberOfLecturers in the solution uses a byte parameter (setNumberOfLecturers(byte numberOfLecturers)), whereas the problem statement and UML indicate the attribute should be an int and other getters/setters are expected to use int. This method parameter type can cause confusion or subtle compilation issues when students implement setters using int as shown in the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the setter signature in the solution to accept an int parameter (public void setNumberOfLecturers(int numberOfLecturers)) to match the UML and attribute type. Alternatively, if a byte is intentionally desired, update the problem statement/UML to indicate byte and document the reason; prefer using int for consistency and to avoid implicit narrowing conversion issues.
